models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B A3B OptiQ 4bit
models.expect: Takes a scoped task from the main agent and returns in seconds. Reads, renames, small edits and single-file changes. Not for work that needs many turns: it is unreliable past the point where a task stops being focused. The OptiQ build is chosen over the plain 4-bit because the plain one produced a roughly 200-call runaway tool loop in both passes at the 36 GB memory cap.

models.name: Qwen 3.8 27B 4bit
models.role: Opt-in alternative, slower and much less predictable
models.expect: Solves about as much as the default and takes roughly seven times longer. Four runs on a repaired benchmark verified 4, 4, 3 and 4 of 8 against the default's 3, 2, 4 and 4 — overlapping ranges, no measurable difference. Median task 58 to 104 seconds against 10 to 12, and it hit the seven-minute cap ten times across those runs where the default hit it once. An earlier version of this text said it solved more; that was measured before a fault was found that stopped every model from compiling or running tests, and the gap did not survive the fix. Offered because people ask for it and because a benchmark of eight tasks is not the last word on a model. If you want an answer in ten seconds, take the default.

models.name: Qwen 3.8 27B 8bit (mlx-lm)
models.role: Opt-in alternative, the quality build, weakest here
models.expect: The build most discussed publicly and the one we can say least about. Two runs on 1 September verified nothing at all, every task timing out having completed zero turns — but a configuration change of ours sits on that result, so we do not report it as the model's. Its earlier runs, under a longer timeout, verified 2 of 8 and 1 of 10. Fits a 48 GB machine at about 27 GB resident, but 30 GB of weights leaves roughly 6 GB for cache under a 36 GB wired limit, so context is capped at 65k against the 4-bit's 131k. If you want one Qwen3.8, take the 4-bit.
